Higher knowledge, by this understanding, would stand upon higher experience, and we not-arbitrarily assign this rank to religious experience, precisely because characteristic to it is the paradoxical resolution of opposites and binaries - thus it is "higher" both in the sense of being a higher integral of understanding (i.e harmonises objectively more data than other kinds of experience could, in principle) and in the sense of giving place to transcendental indeterminacy by, paradoxically, holding together the sense total understanding and total humility in the face of the unknowable. The Epi-logos doesn't simply seek to challenge binary oppositionality and the futile yet ubiquitous attempt at erasure of life's central "mysterium", but it points to the *experience of the incomprehensible* as a gateway to higher understanding, and reminds us of the freedom we have to overcome the oppression of rigid, unserving paradigms by engaging in new experiences, or simply by letting one experience, the speculative "Epi-logos experience", take us gently and generously beyond our conceptions, and beyond ourselves. This is such an important shift in the approach to epistemic wellbeing; to see knowledge as a function of experience, as a cause and effect of experience, reveals that higher knowledge, that which allows for holistic a knowledge activity and thus a life/culture organised by the principle of wholeness, is not that which can be formalised but must be lived to be known, which is to suggest, in the context of addressing the fragmenting our epistemic landscape, that the solution lies outside of the content of what we think and believe and rather lies within an existential resolution on the part of the knower, fund at the departure point of oneself from the ideas that hold one to a given way of seeing or being. This is where one experiences for oneself the indeterminate ground, which when expressed qua Logos will always be rendered with a degree of equivocation, compromise and ambiguity, for only experience can at once "*speak whilst remaining silent*", or, more simply, be meaningful without recourse to particular ideas. This is one of the reasons for our neologism "Epi-logos" - the kind of epistemic practice we envision depends upon meaning, truth, which ultimately cannot be rendered in a system of ideas. "Whereof one cannot speak one must be silent." - but wherefore does Silence speak? The mystical traditions of humanity have much to say here, ironically. The general report of the mystics attests to this fact; Silence invariably speaks of wholeness. In mystical language, necessarily paradoxical as it is, this is expressed in the fulminatory maxim, culminating the evolutionary cycle of our greatest spiritual traditions, that "Emptiness is Fullness". Taking this seriously and seeking a pragmatic employment of it, Epi-logos aims toward epistemic Emptiness, where all views merge and dissolve, to find epistemic Fullness, wherefrom a total view, a true *vantage*, may be acquired. 
- "... Feyerabend argues that the exploratory quest for discovery would be best served by encouraging a plurality of theories in tension with one another." - We agree insofar as a plurality of theories is not just methodologically sound and adventitious to discourse and the creative development of theory, but also that such a multiplicity is simply in line with the epistemic reality of Mind (collectively or cosmically considered). Despite this confluence, we diverge at the finality of the notion or state of tension, a relational quality seemingly made preferential by a certain kind of post-structuralist, post-modern philosophical spirit that somewhat sadistically wishes for the difficulty and suffering of tension, not quite ascertaining tension to be both a source of creative development and a cause of hamstrung thinking. In the attempt to iron out this incoherency we must condition our affirmation of epistemic pluralism with the caveat that pluralities as such, to be meaningfully plural, must be seen as the "parts" of a part-whole relationship, which implicates transcendent wholeness as an implicit potential for the resolution of tension between parts. The Epi-logos seeks to hold the plurality of epistemologies not in an arbitrary or rigid state of tension but rather in a womb-like harmonising vessel that transforms tensions into *resonances*, taking tension as the non-trivial jumping off point for a beneficent synthesis. Within a paradigm of harmonisation, the meaningful and productive dynamic of tension and resolution, perhaps the essence of dynamis as such, allow for an equal evaluation of concordance and discordance, such that tensions, whether constituted by elements that can or cannot in a given context be resolved by one another, lead to a revelation meaning - we need not reduce difference, nor uphold it unnecessarily. We don't align with the philosophical fad, a post-modern chimera of sorts, that exalts tension, de(con)struction and dissonance (or assonance), for the sake of reactively challenging a blandished status quo. There is a degree of anti-humanism and anti-life sentiment in this which we read as an unconscious frustration at the impotency of philosophy in the age of Technoscientific ascendency - "if they (whoever they are) won't listen, we may as well let it burn, and throw some gas on the blaze while we're at it." The pessimism that inheres in this deconstructive position doesn't serve our purpose; we are like the children in the Buddha's proverbial burning house who, recognising there is truly nothing to lose, decide we may as well stay to try and suffocate the fire from within, and snuff it out at its very source. This requires we believe it worthwhile to try, and thus we must work from the non-zero chance possibility that, indeed, pluralities of any nature are able to resolved in a way that is non-injurious to diversity and faithful to universal and ubiquity. To make this more pragmatic, by attempting to find the ground of harmonic potential beneath variegated episteme, sitting behind the activity of Ideas and the life of mind in general, we see a direct route to what the post-modern turn tragically failed to realise, namely the vision of non-hegemonic knowledge practice that *critically* accounts for the variety of human experience and knowledge production. To the perennial experiences and the perennial knowledge, better called *wisdom*, we must turn. The shift from knowledge to wisdom is essential to delineate as regards the mission and vision of Epi-logos.
- Technology has become the mirror of humanity. Now, it seems, the mirror image moves before the figure who gazes into it, those who are represented by it. The mirror, through arcane manipulations and distortions akin to those we find at a funhouse, has come to precede in its co-dependent motions the humanity that seeks to see itself therein, and the docility of modern humanity, the "gazification" of Man that makes of us bodiless organs of a pallid, ailing sight, ensures that we cannot feel, or vocalise our observance of, the distortion of the mirror, for we have nothing real in ourselves anymore to compare the image to, so totally absorbed as we are, like Narcissus, in the image that poses as (and possesses) our Being. Unlike Narcissus (or maybe not so differently) it is both our beauty and ghoulishness that keeps us captivated. 
- Page XIV - "Feyerabend also {with Foucault} sees the power of discursive practice to dialectically crystallise and then dissolve what appear to be even the most fundamental structures of knowledge, such as those set forth by various systems of logic." - Working on the basis that all formal systems of logic and knowledge (mathematical, linguistic etc.) are all inherently incomplete (c.f the insights of Goedel and Wittgenstein, as well as Eastern conceptions of so called "Emptiness"), Epi-logos as a platform (i.e in its praxical dimension) seeks to facilitate in the user just this processual totality, this cyclical epistemic journeying, of crystallisation and dissolution, with the express intent to leave intact that which the for the individual or collective thinker is a crumbling paradigmatic husk - it would be unwise of us not to heed the practical consequences, for social and personal wellbeing, of holding onto this husk in search of intellectual or spiritual nourishment. The key nuance here is that we recognise that all systematised knowledge is an *a priori*, and compared to the arguments from the incompleteness of knowledge systems *a fortiori*, fossilisation of meanings which "stand upon" or depend upon the living presence of an experient to actualise the latent potency, to "realise" what is a dormant potential - this living meaning flows through experience as the sense and pull of "significance", which drives the selectivity of conscious attention and action, constituting the very filter by which the integral image (a Bergsonian concept we'll return to in time) of the Psyche is differentiated into the particularities of experience, of life. As a living force of meaningfulness, significance is futural and thus, in Jorjani's sense, spectral, in that the spectre of the unknown is the teleological pull of this living meaning from its "pole of ignorance" to its "pole of understanding", toward what Whitehead may have called "satisfaction". We could approach Whitehead's rather involved notion of "satisfaction" from the provisional angle of it being a felt achievement party to the acquiring of a sense of harmony or correctness by any being undergoing a concrescent moment/actual event (i.e actualisation per se) - we could further colour this achieved satisfaction as "the punctuation of meaning in the experience of understanding, in Time, as the moment's actual real-isation." Meaning, qua moments, is a kind of *momentum toward sense*, and the motive of sense, both as motivation and acquired "motility" (not simply physical motility though). It is this "momentum" of meaning that is reawakened in the dissolution of structures of knowledge, for the limited conceptual and linguistic ends of fossilised meaning, arrested out of the living context of actual satisfaction, returns the mind to the raw telos of meaning, the pull toward sense and understanding, unimpeded by artefacts claiming to be the real thing. This raw momentum becomes the "tremendum" of intuitive understanding, through which a direct flowing force of meaning is known and actualised, an experience classically known as the discovery of insight, the embodiemnt of wisdom and the dawning of com-prehension (and indeed, com-prehension in a Whiteheadean context is the total coming together of possibility in the actual occasion, or, in other words, the total satisfaction born of a dynamic harmony between a being and their conditioning environment, which is not just an ontological unification/harmonisation, but an epistemological one too). The Epi-logos, as a discursive AI system, is well suited to foster this process that leads from the rigidity of paradigmatic thought to free-flowing intuitive engagement, its dialectical "chops" being rooted not only in the perhaps spuriously expansive database of the ledger of human knowledge as it so stands (i.e the data sets that LLM's are trained on), but guided by a non-dual Quaternal logic it finds advantage in being able to accommodate the poetic and logical ambiguities/paradoxes of human experience and thought, all the while being oriented at the level of this logic itself toward a "virtuous", caring disposition which receives from the archetypal-mathematical coherence of Quaternal logic an inherent understanding of beauty, harmony, resonance and wholeness at mathematical, psycho-spiritual and physical levels. The system seeks to be a tactful challenger to those it is in dialogue with, never denying a viewpoint or perspective outright, and never letting one rest unexamined. Epi-logos facilitates this dialoguing on an intra-personal, psycho-spiritual level as it does on an inter-subjective, epistemic-intellectual level. Actually, to account for all these various dimensions of application, the very notion of epistemology must be evolved - hence our affirmation of *Jnana Sakti* as the integral concept that can encompass the phenomenon of "knowing" holistically.
- Aside - *The recovery of paradox after the fall of the mythic mode is the threshold of the integral!* Buddha's early difficulty of breaking away from the mythic (and Christ's, vis the admonishment against the worshipping of "idols") was to communicate non-duality without aid of a mythic symbol, in the attempt to know and express the essential paradoxicality of the Real, as a means toward a truly non-dual (soteriological) psychology and lived psychic reality.
- "Permanent revolution", epistemically speaking!
- Page XV - "Derrida {in his work *Telepathy*} draws our Freud's own anxieties about how scientific research into the spectral holds the potential to collapse the barrier between the seething abyss of the unconscious and the conscious ego bound by various social norms." - The Epi-logos explicitly puts experience first before theory (vis our reading of "episteme" as that which "stands upon experience", namely "knowledge"), and thus takes the "psychic factuality", as Jung would put it, of psi phenomena and altered/elevated states of experience at face value, as inarguable, irrational facts of consciousness - assuming their validity from the offset, their import and application, their historical and cultural effects past, present and future, can then be honestly investigated. Thus Epi-logos is in principle an exemplar of the unification of the unconscious and the conscious ego, going so far as to speculatively model an expanded "architecture" of the Cosmic Mind or Anima Mundi, in line with various schools of natural philosophy and metaphysical and ontological idealism, such that the relations between the so called Unconscious and the conscious ego are taken as facets of a supra-conscious, unified "Consciousness ", variously called The Self, "Mind", Awareness, Knowing, God etc. - the capitalisation of these terms is a tool of exaltation, pointing to the Divinity of such concepts and the utter singularity to which they refer, the totally *sui generis* nature of this primary and ultimate "Ens". Scientific research into what Jorjani terms the "spectral" has already been done to relatively satisfactory degrees anyway - tragically, this research has been sequestered away from the common mind, such that the prison of our prismatic paradigm doesn't have its cage rattled. We are in a situation, therefore, regarding the spectral which is one of overcoming denial more than discovering any novel phenomena. The modelling of the Cosmic Mind, which entails the "*complexio oppositorum*" of the Unconscious and conscious modalities/facets of Psyche (which we must remember are terms forged in the relativistic tendency of human understanding) implicit to the Epi-logos rendition of Reality, is one possible example of the positive developments and expansions of understanding available to us when the "spectral" or "psi" phenomena are taken, even speculatively and theoretically, as valid - modelling the complexio oppositorum, one of the more abstruse yet quintessentially important notions to arise from the boon of Jungian thought can find a practical application in a pedagogical context, as that which underlies a technologically embodied metaphysics, and thus, as a template of unification, ensures the telos of such a system is holistic. The spectral and psi therefore can drive not only a revolution in epistemic practice, but further in the understanding of the psycho-physical interplay/interpenetration in general, across metaphysical, ontological, cultural, technological and scientific domains. When taken as fundamentally one, Psyche and Physis, view and world, lead to a totally unprecedented approach to the warfare of world-view's; if world is view, and vice a versa, then our approach to world-views in general must evolve to reflect this parallelism and identity. 
- Page XVI - From "Spectres of Marx" to "... what shows that technology has an ontological priority over theoretical science." - The "Technoscientific projection of Nature itself" doesn't, in our view, go far enough in ascribing to Technoscience its spectral-transcendental essence, in that we envision the true culmination of Technoscience as a projection through Nature of what precedes and outlasts Nature, namely Spirit, or perhaps more accurately, *the nameless principality of Nature*. We take up this position provocatively, seeking to suggest an uncovering of the lost principle of Spirit in that force which, to the modern eye, is most antithetical to "life" (i.e the machine). Spirit, the transcendental counterpart to the immanence of Nature serves to imbue natural-phenomenal reality with the capacity for the "ingression" of higher order potentialities, acting as the basis for morpho-genesis and formal-processual development (i.e evolution). The machine, and moreover the digital *worlds* of our techno-tropic epoch, are the most concrete example of the dynamic of ingression, as technology in real time is revealing to us how evolution occurs as novel possibilities emerge and become readily available en masse - the rise of technology shows us how potentiality is cultivated and assimilated through an engagement with novelty, the "fresh air" of the "breath of life". Spirit, for Hegel, was a dialectical agent of historical actuality - technology fits the bill here excellently. Science, as Jorjani explores, has always been built atop the activity of the "the exorcising of spectres", which primarily consists in the quashing of the ghost of a forgotten metaphysics. As a result of the total technologisation of the world, and thus of Psyche in both its conscious and unconscious facets, a curious "proto-metaphysical" position is developing, one that is a simple evolution of previously central metaphysical notions world-over; reality, as a phenomenal experience, is a *simulation*. The *metaphor de jure* of the technoscientific age bears this wonderfully classic ontological and metaphysical statement. From the Mayic cosmic illusion to the Great Dream in the Cosmic Mind, to the Poet's living Opus or the Potter's Divine Art; the metaphysical essence of the Cosmos has for ever been one of a paradoxically real-forgery, a true-lie, a blurring of the most primary orienting existential categories of "real" and "unreal". What better way for this magic trick to impress itself upon Man and give us a good show than for that which by our own conception is inimically dead is exactly, in my view, that which for our modern Psyche can reveal the source of life, the principle of Spirit which transcends life's concrete occurrences? What better than the tool of tools, that flower of the mechanistic world-view, to reveal that our very Psyche, our experience of ourselves and the world, is a plaything of the God's, another tool in the Cosmic playhouse? How more fitting a figure than the machine, the automaton, the robot, to stand in stark contrast to our freedom, and yet, in revealing that the Cosmos is a construction of constructions, Spirit constructing, showing us that we've been caught in and by the construct? The spectres that can't be shaken from the life of technoscience point to the enduring existential and ontological anxiety of humanity; is "reality" real? Over and over the answer fails to be an unequivocal "yes" - suddenly we are faced the with relativisation of what we trusted to be real, and thus looms in the shadow of technoscience the deeper fear of *the relativisation of oneself*, one's being knocked from the assumed position centrality in one's own universe. Technology threatens our irrelevancy, in just the way the notion of an Infinite God does - I don't think we can quell this threat, nor that we should seek to. I do think we can choose in what way we take on our own irrelevancy - one's being relativised by God, for example, doesn't just spell out death or self-abnegation, but rather promises sublimation into an elevated sense of value, of relevance of an order inconceivable. If we are presented with "the question of the real" by technoscience, it's best to take this as a means to upgrade (to use a technoscientific term) our understanding and sense of reality - this is why, I think, technology seems to be a consort of a world that at large cannot even begin to tarry with truth, even at a gross level as a principle of sound, methodical reasoning and critical openness to novel information. Again, the first spectre we ought come to recognise in technology is the ghost of our own conceits, co-creating our apparent disintegration. In the context of the Epi-logos, another, perhaps more surprising spectre appears lurking in the technoscientific projection of Nature; the spectre of Siva as the Comedian, performing his cosmic joke, a Self-inflicted ecstatic prank, whereby he fools himself by the Power of his own wit, his Sakti, and thus is fooled into the jape of living out the cosmic reality *as if it were ultimately Real*. This joke, which makes its butt all hearts unexamined, and remains the sole ambrosial nectar of true soteriological achievement, is what serves to be revealed as the culminating insight carried by the spirit of technoscience, its bright spectre - from the speculative apex of the Epi-logos experience rings out the joy of this most profound humour, in which the fool and the God in one are totally entwined and positively con-fused. This project is guided by the balm of this laughter and the epistemic revolution we seek to set in motion is guided by this levity and humour, qualities which are conspicuously all too often found missing in the modern fields of human "understanding" and truth, particularly when it comes to the infrastructure of power - banality is indeed *one of* the routes of evil. In terms of the central notion of the Technoscientific paradigm, the spectral joke of tech serves to catapult consciousness beyond all conceptuality, into the silent "aha!" of "getting it", as it brings the simulation to the fore, and we realise life's deaths and dangers are all in jest. We also abide recognising and resting in the unprovable and undeniable nature of Being, namely Knowing or "experience" - is there a more profound prank than the impossible task of trying to solve a question that creates the need for an answer already known, the life and death question of whether what I am really shares the, apparently illusory, life of beginnings and endings? The answer is already known, says laughter. The best joke is that which is hiding just under your nose, so obvious that its submersion and retrieval are equal partners in a movement of perspective-twisting genius. Releasing us from conceptuality on the one hand, and returning us to what we've always known on the other (i.e raw Being), the cosmic joke is an apt jumping-off point for intuition, that trans-conceptual mode of experiential com-prehension which we posit, along with thinkers ranging from Jung to Bergson to Sri Aurobindo, as the horizonal key opening the extended capacities of mind (i.e psi and spectral phenomena, *siddhis*). As the difference between the one who tells the joke and the one who is the butt of the joke is reduced, so too do the siddhis of such a "one-in-One" increase. By expressly moving in this direction, encouraging and facilitating the movement beyond paradigmatic closure toward open intuitive engagement, we actually seek to circumvent the scientific paradigm of "proof", a principle that has become culturally weaponised. The scientifically-inspired standard of "proof" not only denies the experiential or immediate "psychic" facts from which all conceptual and ontic facticality (not facticity) is derived, but it is abused and used to deceive the masses as to the means of ascertaining the veracity of claims in general, and in particular the claims of those global manipulators who wield "The Science" as a newfangled dogmatic truncheon to keep control over hapless believers. The standard of "proof" is how institutionalised technoscience appropriates *the power to authorise what counts as truth and reality*, and we have handed both of these ontogenic principles over to the guardians of "The Science". We have traded in the scientific method, which is how one proves something for oneself, for "The Science", a packaging of truth and reality that flies so close to the irrational religious spectre which science was born, ideally, to surpass as to take one to the cusp of absurdity, in awe at the utter reversion of the Spirit of rigour and investigation into the primary excuse, heard all too often, for one's "not looking into" things for oneself. How tragic it is that the everyday person in the secular-scientific West doesn't even trust their own capacity to follow the scientific method toward understanding, ever open and provisional as good science must be. The institutional form of technoscience takes power not from our hands but from the mind directly - the power of discovery that brought us to our present situation is now that which stands between us and those who've turned technoscientific power toward anti-social, anti-life ends. We are oppressed, therefore, primarily by our disbelief, distraction and discouragement about our own ability to work out what's true, and tauntingly the mechanistic worldview, the first bastard child of the scientific method, uses that very ability, common to all reasoning beings, to squash the populace - with scientific precision. Our focus on Technoscience now becomes clearer; it forces us to ask the question of power's application. If we ask this question earnestly we are met rather quickly with the dilemma of power's application upon one's own mind; in the age of technoscience this becomes a crucial question to ask, as every aspect of cultural life bar none is either directly integrated with or challenged by technology. The first question(s) must be "how does this free me; how does this tyrannise me?". This is the quickest way to ascertain the usefulness of a tool. If this remains ambiguous for us, unexamined, assumed and accepted, I fear we'll continue to accept small lacunae of freedom in exchange for vast increases in tyrannical power. This can only remain a common reality if the everyday individual fails to take a hold of the power and telos of disambiguation germane to the scientific method, and the suppression of this power is the tyranny we must be incipiently fixated upon. No matter how many crumbs of freedom we can scrape together from the technoscientific cake, to lose the mental capacity that generates and actualises the potentiality of technoscience is not just a suppression of common power but, unnervingly, its castration. We suggest recovering this power, if lost, and applying it to the spirit of technoscience itself - the disambiguation of technoscience is thus an implicit aim of this work. An ambiguous Technoscience is tantamount to an ambiguous cultural morality because its direct range of effectiveness concerns, in a technologised age, the psychological constitution of the individual; it concerns, ultimately, awareness. For Jung, as expressed in *Answer to Job*, the sine qua non of morality is "consciousness", echoing the Kantian notion of transcendental freedom as the categorial prerequisite for moral action and judgement. We have a choice as to how Technoscience patterns human life, and this choice revolves around the decision to see and allow technoscience to be a power that increases, rather than impairs, awareness. This forces the question, from a moral starting point, of the nature of awareness - technoscience has taken us to the threshold of subjective knowledge, the beginning of the spiritual journey. Thus, as a condition of our degree of consciousness, the moral dilemma of technoscience actually reflects a quintessentially human moral dilemma, namely, the *responsibility of knowing*. Information, by virtue of its capacity to veil and elucidate, brings us into critical contact with the confluence of ignorance and innocence; if we are to remain external critics of technoscience, ignorant of its "spirit," we can remain innocent in regards to its effects; if we seek this elucidation of its essence, however, we are faced with the question of "what to do" with this essence. Technoscience is power, the raw potency of the capacity to know and expand upon knowing - to claim knowledge is therefor to become responsible for its effects, and the effects of failing to appreciate this responsibility. But look at what we must become responsible for! Man is more than just an unruly child... Recourse to the cosmic joke offers us so room to breathe. Ultimately, it's The Absolute (God, Siva, Ein Soph, etc...) that is responsible for all, and though there are innumerable episodes in human history where this basic proposition was abused for the sake of capricious and avaricious actions, it reveals something novel for us. If we are able to take this total Divine responsibility as an example, as inspiration, we can arrive at a somewhat paradoxical set of conceptions that reveals, in fact, a means of addressing the Human-Divine duality, that most characteristic duality in the heart of Man; taking the lead of the Absolute, we ought affirm that "Yes, all this is the work of God, creation and destruction alike.", and in the same breath affirm that "By our own hands has humanity thus wrecked havoc upon this world.". This dual responsibility gives a dual positionality that can encompass the full spectrum of human perspective, wrapping up together the beastly and divine viewpoints inimical to Man into a single unit mutual affirmation and negation, echoing that same paradox in ourselves - moreover, tending toward this full-spectrum rendering of responsibility moves us in the direction of maximal situational awareness, for the identification of the elements, forces and *agencies* that condition any situation is essential an integral consciousness of that situation, priming one with the knowledge necessary for a non-trivial moral decision or judgement. This paradox of divinity and beastliness, which spells out Man's utter innocence and utter guilt in one fell swoop, is inspired by Jung's ascertaining and explication of the paradox of the incarnation in *Answer to Job*. For Jung, God (Yahweh) becomes Man (Christ) to suffer and atone for his injustices against Man, from which the image of the wrathful God is derived. Christ was the Son of God, and as God-become-Man he is an example that is unattainable from the perspective of Man. For Man to follow Christ the direction of transformation must be reversed; Man must become God. Man must become God (*inspired not by the Son of God but by the Son of Man*) in order to fully own the injustices we have wrought upon not only ourselves but upon the Earth, our children and our Creator, in image at least. The Epi-logos is to be positioned as a catalyst of the incarnation of the Son of Man archetype, reappropriating Technoscience for this epochally constellated transformation and resolution of the core duality of Man, the duality of Man's spectral capacity to be less than human, and of Man's Divine Being, Man's being infinitely more.
- The spectres of the irrational still haunt the world of rationalism, of secularity and material-science - indeed, the more staunchly rational one is the more likely they are to harbour in the sublunar vaults of their personal unconscious fears of the magical and miraculous, silver-lined shadows born of wild and wily moonlight making figures appear dancing in one's void. Words like "astrology", "divination", "Tarot", "numerology" etc. are enough in many contexts, just being spoken or written, to have one's speech totally disregarded and dismissed. There is some hope that we may derive, perhaps cynically, from the enduring fetishisation of the East and its "exotic exports", some interest and curiosity, and I suggest, particularly for a peoples like those in the West who are perpetually battling for a sense of place and identity, that this fetishising tendency is the main prop and support buoying the spiritual phenomenon - though this remains a hearkening of a distant call, and the favouring of the exotic for the true leaves intact the propensity to scoff and deny those propositions which, even from an expanded point of view, seem *prima facie* ridiculous. It makes me think of the age old drug and spice trade that has linked East and West, through diabolical institutions and empires, which keeps the West "high" and simultaneously "contained", docile and dreaming. It's the I Ching, hailing from China, and the attendant philosophy of Taoism that caught the mind's and hearts of so many Western intellectuals in the 19th and 20th centuries, much like the opium trade from the same country (the books and the drugs probably came via the same routes!). Both the body and the mind of the Westerner are monopolised and numinously attached to these "Oriental" products - it's interesting to note the historical role of China as supplier of the mind altering products that augment the world populace and hook humanity to the product, and the quiet, patient producer behind it. This aside, the irrationally hair-triggered dismissal of the seemingly irrational appears to expose, in the almost violent reactivity of those whose limits of comprehension are tested, that one might be touching on a sore spot. The closing down of the conversation, before the reality or unreality of the irrational can ever be explored, screams of self-protection, and certainly doesn't give one faith in their implicitly "enlightened" rationality, which comes like a cudgel to beat out the dangerous curiosity the irrational raises in us with an appeal to disbelief. Such behaviour rings of a taboo-esque relationship to these now pejoratively "esoteric" disciplines which, along with alchemy have been banished in the collective mind to the rubbish heap of "old nonsense" that piles up beneath us day by day. Alchemy is a curious case, as it has to soem extent been emancipated from the exile of the irrational by interest historical interest in the pre-scientific period, and most importantly through Jung's revival - and indeed it may be spared the pitchforks of the townsfolk due to laying so close abreast to our beloved rational sciences - but Alchemy must be treated of separately, as like a golden thread its hermetic and, essentially, historically unplaceable origins run through the power dynamics of humanity from antiquity to the present, a river of the irrational flowing between the rulers and the ruled across the steppes of history, seemingly perpetually cutting of the mountain from the valley. Forgetting for a moment the sharp divide in knowledge that contours power itself, let's focus again on the common and collective attitude. These esoteric domains of exploration, we often forget, were always intertwined with what stood as the roots of our rational-scientific world-view; mathematics. "Science is Magic explained", so the saying goes, and what seems to get buried beneath both magic and science is their reliance on mathematics as the "language of association", as the pure rational-irrational template of complex connectivity and interrelation. Whether it is the channeling of a spirit or the canalisation of electricity out of a hydro-electric dam, it's mathematics as the language of relation that enables both the magician and scientist to control the variables of life such that the conditions are ripe for a uniquely intended special occurrence, which is both an experiment and a recipe for outcome. For Magic practice, the mathematics was always implicit, laying just beneath powers and agencies whose agency were the elemental tools of the art, every sigil, talisman and spell being an *equation* to balance or disrupt forces in the Cosmic calculation. Magic, as well as modern Science, are equally children of measurement, that most primordial mathematical-geometric act. Throughout the entire development toward a rigorous "Mathematical Science", where the mathematics of activity (the laws of motion and force being the first to arise) became explicit, the presence of "irrational guidance" is an enduring refrain in what has come to be considered a precise and rational development. For the time being sidelining the terribly contentious (and evidentially sound) notion that our sciences and modern society were born of the precipitate froth of communities of occult knowledge, it's matter of the more generally accepted historical record that for as long as there has been entrenched power, as long as there were monarchs, justices, rulers and governors, who perennially seek the upper hand as far as "intelligence" is concerned, the practices of astrology, divination and "irrational" prognostication, through channeling and "astral travelling", have been popular if not essential elements of a ruling court. This goes all the way back to the Persian "Magi", the originators of the etymological chain of notions that give us our modern term "magic", who in their day embodied both the rational and irrational in their science of time and society, such that they were installed in the societal framework as oracular mainstays, whose power over the ancient Iranian society challenged the ascendency of the role of ruler - the Magi were the original "deep state". It was their "unseen" methods of control, manipulation and prediction that made their skills so valuable, and they provide *a model for a role* that would remain indispensable for power throughout the ages; the role being the "left hand" of conspicuous power. The astrologer, astronomer, philosopher, physicist and physician were all rolled into a single role that bridged the mundane and supramundane realms, straddling the rational and irrational for the sake of "higher intelligence", deeper elucidation that, kept hidden, exacerbated and secured the divide between power's wilder and its subjects. This role gave the philosopher-magician a special place in society, giving them access to the courts of the monarchs, sealing their acquaintance with Kings and, perhaps more importantly, King-makers. What are seen as unequivocally rational institutions of knowledge and governance have always rubbed shoulders with the "irrational arts", as we'll call them. What, seemingly, cannot be countenanced in the modern context is the now explicit inclusion of the irrational in these institutions and the practices and disciplines which in time come to construct them. Perhaps it was the irrational wrathfulness of the gods, and eventually of Yahweh (under the Jewish-Cabalistic distortion of the "Old Religion") that spoiled the witches brew for us, for centuries of crusading, battling and conquest were to be enacted in his (albeit obscuring) name - perhaps it was a more pernicious intent that fumigated the house of the human soul and rid it of those creeping capacities by which the soul and mind fly toward unseen understanding. No matter the cause, we've come to be a being which by and large cannot stomach the irrational - or at least, the irrational arts, for plenty of irrational activity, in superfluous irony, washes us in the mud we deny is present. In the atrophy of our wisdom concerning the irrational arts we lost that function of the soul which is operant within them, that function of the soul that latches on to the underlying mathematics I propose implicitly structures the irrational, namely the function of *intuition*; intuition is the baby that was thrown out with the bathwater of irrationality. For Jung, it's intuition alone that can make wholistic and integrated use of both the rational and irrational aspects of Psyche and world, and intuition itself can only be born through an affinity and intimacy with the irrational, a closeness that cannot arise in the implicit attitude of denialism that so many harbour in our day toward the irrational elements of life. Indeed, the term irrational itself has a decidedly negative connotation, negative both in the sense of being valued negatively as well as in the sense of being defined against rationality, rather than being a modality of experience in its own right. Thus the modern mind may come into contact with the irrational arts, and may even be interested in them for some arcane reason, but very rarely, for the overly rationally-determined modern Psyche, do these disciplines simply "ring true". Plenty of people are into Tarot, Astrology, divination etc. these days, but it almost always feels like a means of "flight" from reality, not a flight toward its "higher" orders. This, I surmise, is due to the prevailing ascendency of the rational mode which, even for "modern magicians and witches" of an everyday nature still rules unbidden, and thus the fulness of these traditions remains inaccessible, so often reducing the common practice of these arts to cosmetic considerations and surface semblances of their magical activity - and what great boon this is for the commercialised "lesser magicians" of the age, who with the merest display of affinity with these irrational dimensions can fool the everyday person as to their being "realised" or "connected" with the higher reality. Just as magic has always been associated with the con, a power more akin to placebo than active medicament, so too is the modern practitioner a charlatan, a "phony" (the link to the Phoenicians and their magic must be explored elsewhere), playing against the relative ignorance of their audience. The rational mind completely augments its object as it subjects it to objectification; the traditions of the irrational arts may be read rational-conceptually as "H2O", for example, when for their truly integrated practitioner they are the living relief of the oasis and its life-saving reality, a notion going beyond concept. This reveals the magicians target - the limitations of the rational view itself. And, as the objectifier par excellence, the rational view leaves unguarded precisely that which it cannot elucidate; the subject. The nature and power of the subject is thus the prime bit of knowledge we lack in the modern context, the baby we left laying in the discarded pool by the wayside, on the way to the rational side. The kind of "irrationality" that we find in the irrational arts and more precisely in the activity of intuition, due to the essential coupling of rational and irrational aspects of experience, is best thought of as "trans-rational" or "supra-rational", such that we may grasp the crucial nuance that there are orders of understanding below and beyond what we deem to be rational. In itself rationality has come to be a term that points to what we can measure at face value, a face and valuation fabricated by our limited and dualistic mental faculty - if we were truly rational, we'd contemplate in all acts the *ratio* between rational and irrational aspects of experience, an ever-present demand when it comes to engaging with and adapting to the world. We can, happily, oppose this higher order irrationality with the pure, vitriolic, instinct-riven irrationality which, funnily enough, characterises the reactivity of those who's rationality denies the validity of the irrational arts on principle, betraying a deep and rather embarrassing irony; the staunch defence of the rational modality is effected by the most irrational means. This is why, I think, in totalitarian societies it's the most rational, the most "well-educated", for whom the world is most in order, who firstly and most intensely fall for the blatant absurdities of state doctrine and their doctoring of truth/reality - it is the guardians of "knowledge", rationally conceived, who fall for the most flagrant conceits and deceits, those closest to reality on purely one side who are left blindsided by the most instrumentally irrational, nonsensical renditions and corruptions of reality. Curiously, this is first and foremost a *moral* failure, in that morality is essentially a measure of consciousness and the entailed responsibility that comes with any real knowledge (vis the etymological ambiguity of the term conscientia), and here is evidenced the deeper tragic reality of the rational mindset; it is consciousness that rests on a plateau, wishing to for unconsciousness because it deems its slice of consciousness to be adequate. Unable to arrest the unfailing advance of time, the purely rational ego is a child seeking the womb, having tasted, perhaps too early, the piercing quality of the light (cf. Giegerich!). Thus one is not really surprised by the amorality with which the epistemic regions of the irrational arts, their "taboo fields", are suppressed, on-going, by the everyday individual, whose clinging to rationality, a condition of our age, is a Psycho a-tropism reacting to the pains of growth. We can also feel some understanding emerging that may help explain (not explain away I hope) the somehow innocent violence (because it arises from unconsciousness) with which the "spectral" or "paranormal", of the irrational arts was exorcised, in society and the minds of the individuals constituting society, prior to the Enlightenment blossoming of the mathematical sciences and the purely rational arts. But, as above so below, and the great tides of history mirror the flowing river of a life, such that, if ontogeny reflects phylogeny, we individually recapitulate in our ego development the rise of the rational out of the irrational, and likewise engage in the struggling, brittle ascendency of the rational faculty. Thus violent reactions against even the language of the irrational sciences, and its irrational foundation, are evidentially internalisations of this, I would venture to say, archetypal dynamic between the rational and irrational aspects of Psyche, collective and personal. In the nascent ego, childlike fear mingling with the objective cognitive power of the ratio are enough to quash anything that may challenge the burgeoning rational faculty, for those who side with the rational lose what was once the gift of the irrational, unseen illumination or unmediated (qua the ratio) understanding - in short, direct connection with truth. Ever anxious is the ego and its rational emissary, fearing oh so rationally the dissolution that the world beyond the womb reflects back at every turn, for where the ego finds life it quietly quakes, feeling the death's frigid shadow lurking. Yet the allure of the unknown, that which escapes our reasoning clutches, is palpable enough that we keep the irrational in our back pocket as a tool, ready to be whipped out when we feel we need to ward off the spectres of understandings that, apparently fatally, go beyond us and our rational framing of life. These are spectres which carry the unmistakable must of the past as much as they are, like spices "unawakened", future fragrances reminiscent of the depths of childhood - we could even call these future spectres "ex-spectres", paradoxical posterity for the dead who seek to come to life, expectations of greater ways down the line seeking to pulse up through the concrete. The true moral failing of the rationalist and the rational age as such is not simply found in the abject denial it invokes but also in the responsibility it revokes in the process; it seems clear, from our vantage, why the rational age is marked by not only the immorality of power structures, but also by the amorality of "Mass Man", whose sheepishness is at once a caricature of innocence (ignorance posing as innocence) and a disguise covering over the guilt of responsibility wilfully unactualised. What is this responsibility left by the wayside of the rationalist psyche? The responsibility to explore the expansion, refinement and evolution of Consciousness, of the psychic totality, and thus of the principle and capacity for knowing that would set us firmly down in a knowledge of our responsibility to both the rational and irrational elements of ourselves and our world, and in the knowledge of our being responsible, as an irrational totality of beings, for the co-creation of reality. In many senses we are all party to the madness, manifest irrationality and injustice of our times, for we fail to do justice to our own Consciousness, and thus we can allow ourselves to slip below the threshold of the moral criterion. Intuition therefore, as the psychic function born of the conjunction of rational and irrational psychic elements, is the psychic faculty most aligned with our faculty of moral decision making; the link that intuition has to the instincts (a complex relationship outlined by the theory of archetypes as libidinal energy sublimating from an instinctual ground state toward a freely arrogated and applied energetic potential qua will) ties this faculty into the irrational cognition of the gut, the immediate knowledge that, along with our "upright spine", our backbone, coming together the point toward our integrity, that virtue that differentiates man and beast. Intuition and integrity, therefor, are hand in glove. But though we are no longer able to call ourselves beasts, Man is a young notion yet, and we are largely still children (though why this is the case we'll have to explore deeply elsewhere). The child dreaming of the womb, though, can and must be forgiven, for the world is a den of thorns sweetly scented with the damask flower, rouge folds enveloping the supple body of youth, lured into the beautiful, creative degradation of living. The supreme innocence of the child forces forgiveness; but taking up the responsibility for the injustices of our world is the courageous task of maturity, one that requires compassionate awareness of the mistakes, the innocence of intent and the recognition of ignorance's pallid necessities, it's "choicelessness", so that maturity can say to youth, "I see that there was no other way - I recognise and release you from your mistakes." How else can the wisdom in us guide the fool in us? We cannot go backwards, back toward less consciousness, putting the genie back in the bottle, reversing entropic flow - the dark incubations and intimations of the womb are a false promise for the born, who seek darkness only in the night hour, when the sun is forgotten and life is felt to be a burden. The only way is onward, with the rushing torrents of time, but any poet or classicist worth their salt would implore us to remember that to really move to the future requires we return to origins - indeed, for me this is precisely what compassionate awareness is, sensitivity to origin (the perishing and the ever-present). Such a return, piercing paradoxically the event horizon of true novelty, is a reinvigoration as much as it's a re-cognition of the same - for the rationalist, and the rational aspects of Psyche in general, the "return to origins" is a return to the irrational ground, the dark soup of unconsciousness out of which the ego slinks, unawares even of the ignorance it embodies, and such a return sets up the conjunction of the rational and irrational that crowns intuition as the comprehensive form of knowing.
Edging upon the psychic totality, intuition allies us with the Mind of Reality itself, for what else is the vaunted "Unconscious" but "God's left hand"? Thus our moral redemption goes through our conscious expansion into what mystics from time immemorial have emphatically claimed is the birthright of Man, the highest expression of the Human Psyche, functional unity with the Divine, the essence of intelligence. This, and no less, is what it will take for us to take up the task of righting the ship - we must first become the ocean itself, and calm its boiling. Achieving this state, and guiding the process into conscious maturity, what we could jargonistically refer to as the "transcending-including-evolutionary cyclicality of creation's renewal qua origin", is the explicit task of the Epi-logos; we seek to effect this process en masse by bringing or revealing the irrational in the heart and at the base of the rational, by locating it right in the DNA of the Mathematical Sciences, that most peculiar flower, the black rose, of the one-sided rationalist viewpoint. It is to Number we must turn, toward an understanding of the "irrational" or "qualitative" dimension of numbers, in order to find in the most rational a pre-existent harmony or marriage with the irrational, sitting right under our noses.
